chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Saeed al-A'raj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When the Quraish demolished the Ka'bah, they found a stone in its foundations containing a writing which they could not read properly, until they called a man who read it, and it said: 'I am Allah, the Lord of Bakka. I sanctified it on the day I created the heavens and the earth, and I placed it between these two mountains, and I surrounded it with seven angels, encircling it.'

key_terms.الْكَعْبَة: The Ka'bah, the cube-shaped building in Mecca
key_terms.بَكَّة: Bakka, an ancient name for Mecca

ai.seo_question: What did the Quraish find inside the foundation of the Ka'bah when they demolished it?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the pre-existence and divine sanctity of the Ka'bah, asserting that its consecration predates the creation of the heavens and earth. It underscores the theological significance of the site as a sanctuary protected by seven angels, reinforcing its status as the spiritual axis of the world in Shia tradition.
